column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah the Exalted said: Whoever is hostile to an ally of Mine, I have declared war against him. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory on him,

and My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary deeds until I love him. When I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes and his foot with which he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him; and if he seeks refuge with Me, I will surely grant him refuge.” Reported by al-Bukhārī.
ʿĀdā (“is hostile”): from muʿādāh (hostility), the opposite of muwālāh (alliance). In one narration: “Whoever insults…”
Waliyyan (“an ally”): one who knows Allah, keeps constantly to obeying Him and is sincere in worshipping Him.
“I have declared war against him”: I have informed him that I am at war with him.
ʿAbdī (“My servant”): this attribution is for honour.
Yataqarrabu ilayya (“draws near to Me”): seeks nearness to Me. In one narration: “seeks My love”.
Bi-l-nawāfil (“with voluntary deeds”): voluntary acts of every kind of worship.
“I become his hearing…” to the end: what is meant is that these faculties are protected from being used in disobedience, so he does not hear what the Sharīʿah has not permitted him to hear,

does not see what it has not permitted him to see, does not stretch out his hand to anything it has not permitted him to reach for, and does not strive except in what the Sharīʿah has permitted striving for.
La-uʿṭiyannahu (“I will surely give him”): what he asked for.
“And if he seeks refuge with Me (istaʿādhanī)”: with the nūn of protection; it is also narrated with the single-dotted bāʾ (istaʿādha bī), and the first is better known.
La-uʿīdhannahu (“I will surely grant him refuge”): from what he fears.
Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, has given prior warning to everyone who is hostile to an ally [of His] that He has declared that He is at war with him, by the very hostility.

This does not include what circumstances sometimes require of dispute between two allies of Allah the Exalted in a legal case or a dispute aimed at bringing out an unclear right, for this has happened among many of the allies of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
Performing the obligations is the most beloved of deeds to Allah the Exalted, because of what they display of the greatness of lordship and the humility of servitude.
A voluntary deed is accepted only when the obligation has been performed, since it is called “voluntary” (nāfilah, “additional”) only once the obligation has been fulfilled.

The allies of Allah the Exalted are those who draw near to Him with what brings them near to Him; this shows the falsity of the claim that there is a path to alliance with Allah other than drawing near to Allah the Exalted through the acts of obedience He has prescribed.

Whoever does what is obligatory on him and draws near with voluntary deeds, Allah grants him success so that he does not hear what the Sharīʿah has not permitted, does not see what he has not been permitted to see,
does not stretch out his hand to anything the Sharīʿah has not permitted him to reach for, and does not strive except in what he has been permitted to strive for.
This is what is meant by His words, “I become his hearing…” to the end, not what the proponents of union (ittiḥād) and indwelling (ḥulūl) claim.
Exalted is Allah above what they say.
Whoever reaches the station mentioned has his supplication answered.
However high a servant rises in rank, he never ceases asking his Lord, because of the humility before Him and display of servitude in that.
